reasons.A: Closest movement: short, complete, plain declaratives with even rhythm, dry understatement ('I doubt it.') and a flat, understated close; only the 'not really a box of chores' summary line reaches further than the author does.
reasons.C: Right flat, dry stance and concrete deadpan ('I know. I walked past it this morning.'), but it stacks fragments more heavily than the author and packs them into long paragraphs, where the author uses short ones.
reasons.B: Short sentences fit, but it keeps reaching for neat aphoristic closers ('The list noticed first.', 'That is why I trust it.', 'It has room for more.') and lyrical lines ('read the seasons in the ink') that are more literary than the author's deadpan.
reasons.D: Long, flowing, subordinated sentences, colons, and an essayistic, reflective register ('The first thing that jumps out', 'quietly noticed') unlike the author's clipped plain statements.
